Our Story|

With 30 years of legacy in creating leaders, the Pune Institute of Computer Technology (PICT) now brings to you PICT Model School. This futuristic educational establishment has been meticulously designed and planned to offer one of its kind learning experience to the 21st Century learners.

Nestled in a safe and secured environment, ensuring emotional and physical protection is our priority. All children are treated equally and respected for their uniqueness. Children are trained to understand their environment intuitively and deal with situations independently.

Our classrooms are active learning hubs; wherein learners are actively engaged in exploring concepts. Learning by Doing is the Mantra at school. We are gearing up our learners to become lifelong independent learners with a love for seeking, sharing, and applying knowledge in the true sense. We are looking at skill ready, employable young citizens who will walk their way through life with confidence. We are building young entrepreneurs in our learning hubs, we are opening up minds.

Our Vision

To impart education that fosters global citizenship with values deep rooted in our culture and providing learning opportunities to tap potential of every individual in a stimulating environment, where tradition meets technology.

Our Mission

To provide stimulating and innovative tools and techniques through modern infrastructure, befitting individual learning needs and empowering them to meet the challenges of education, work and life in a rapidly changing global scenario.

Willing to Unlearn and Relearn?

With India moving steadily towards competency-based education, educators must upskill themselves to stay relevant and employable. If you have the time and commitment to deepen your conceptual knowledge and hone your applied thinking, if you are a strong believer in equitable and inclusive education, if your focus is on 'how to learn' rather than only 'what to learn', if your happiness lies in sharing than hoarding and if your success is in passing on your skills to the future generations, we will train you to shift from a culture of rote memorisation as learning to achievement of mastery in competencies.
To be the Torchbearers as envisaged by the National Education Policy 2020 at PICT Model School, look through the subject-specific prerequisites given below.


Preparatory Stage and Middle Stage Secondary Stage Admin
  1. Home Room Teachers (For Grades 1 & 2): Graduate with a B.Ed from any recognized university in India with a deep conceptual understanding of English, EVS and Math.
  2. English: Graduate in/with English and having English as one of the methodologies in B.Ed. A Certificate / Diploma in Teaching & Learning / CELTA Certificate / Certificate in TESOL will be an added advantage.
  3. Science: Graduate in/with Science and having Science as one of the methodologies in B.Ed.
  4. Social Science: Graduate in/with Geography / History / Political Science / Economics and having at least one of the Social Science subjects as a methodology in B.Ed.
  5. Mathematics: Graduate in or with Math and having Math as one of the methodologies in B.Ed.
  6. Computer Science: Graduate in with Computer Science / Computer Applications / Information Technology or Graduate with Mathematics and a Diploma in IT from any recognized university.
  7. Hindi: Graduate in/with Hindi and having Hindi as one of the methodologies in B.Ed.
  8. Marathi: Graduate in/with Marathi and having Marathi as one of the methodologies in B.Ed.
  9. Sanskrit: Graduate in/with Sanskrit and having Sanskrit as one of the methodologies in B.Ed. / Pandit training.
  10. French: Graduate in/with French / Diploma in Teaching French / having at least B2 Level DELF Certificate.
  11. German: Graduate in/with German / Diploma in Teaching German / having at least B2 Level Goethe- Zertificat Certificate / DaF Certificate.
  12. Vocal Music: Graduate in/with Music and Sangeet Visharad Certificate from any recognized university.
  13. Dance: Graduate in/with Classical Dance / Diploma in Classical Dance from any recognized university.
  14. Art: Post-graduate in Fine Arts/ Graduate in Fine Arts with Painting or Drawing specialization from any recognized university.
  15. Counsellor: Graduate in Psychology / Post-Graduate in Child Development / Graduate with Diploma in Career Guidance and Counselling.
  16. Special Educator: Graduate in Psychology with a B.Ed in Special Education.
  17. Librarian: Post-Graduate / Graduate with a degree/diploma in Library Science from a recognized university. Candidates should have good communication skills and should possess the art of inspiring a love for reading in young minds.

  4. Chemistry: Post Graduate in Chemistry/Bio-Chemistry from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation in/with Chemistry/Bio-Chemistry or M.Sc.   5. Biology: Post Graduate in Zoology/Botany/Physiology from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation in/with Zoology/Botany/Physiology or M.Sc.   6. Economics: Post Graduate in Economics from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation in/with Economics and a strong base in Mathematics/Statistics. Having a B.Ed. in Economics as one of the methodologies will be an advantage.
  7. History: Post Graduate in History from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation in/with History. Having a B.Ed. with History as one of the methodologies will be an advantage.
  8. Geography: Post Graduate in Geography from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation in/with Geography. Having a B.Ed. in Geography as one of the methodologies will be an advantage.
  9. Accounts: Masters in Commerce with Accountancy, from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation / B.Ed. from a recognized Institute.
  10. Business Studies: Masters in Commerce with Business Studies from any recognised university in India or abroad with Graduation/ B.Ed. from a recognized Institute.
  11. Entrepreneurship: Masters in Commerce with Entrepreneurship from a recognized University / B.Ed. from a recognized Institute.
  12. Financial Market Management: M.Com./ MBA / MA in Economics / Masters in Financial Management / Masters in Financial Services / Equivalent for Accounting for Business / Bachelor Degree from a recognized Institute with NSE’s Certification in Financial Markets NCFM.
  13. Commercial Arts: MA in Fine Arts (with Commercial Art or Applied Arts Specialization). Intermediate / Higher Secondary / Senior School Secondary with 5 years of experience / Diploma in Commercial Arts from a recognized Institute or University.
  14. Psychology: Graduate/Post Graduate in Psychology / Post Graduate in Child Development or Graduate/Post Graduate with Diploma in Career Guidance and Counselling.
  15. Applied Mathematics: M.Sc. in Mathematics/B.Ed. from an institution recognized by NCTE.
  16. Computer Science: BE, B.Tech. in Computer Science / Computer Engineering / Masters in Information Technology / B.Sc. (Computer Science), M.Sc. (Mathematics), MCA / B.Ed. from NCTE.

Knowledge of local Indian languages, proficiency in English and MS Office, readiness for frequent travels and possessing a positive attitude towards learning and training are a must.

  4. Front Office Executive: Graduate with excellent communication skills, good interpersonal and liaison skills, working knowledge of computers and a pleasant personality.
  5. Lab Assistant: Graduate with good communication skills and at least 3 years of experience in similar profiles from reputed organisation.
  6. Data Entry Operator: Graduate with proficiency in MS Office, Photoshop, Designing and Publishing software with a typing speed of at least 80 words per minute. Typing knowledge in Hindi and Marathi script will be an advantage.
  7. Librarian: A Bachelor degree in Library Science / Graduate with a one-year diploma in Library Science from a recognized Institution.

Procedure

    Step 1: Fill in the application form with the required details (Note: all the fields need to be filled in)

    Step 2: Scrutiny of application form and verification of documents. Resume with current photo, self attested photocopies of all relevant documents need to be attached with the application form.

    Step 3: Taking a written assessment comprising three parts: General Aptitude, Teaching Aptitude and Subject Specific Assessment.

    Step 4: Upon scoring 80% and above, a demo will be scheduled on a mutually agreed timing.

    Step 5: Based on the success of the demo, a final interview with the Principal will be scheduled to discuss the job profile, terms and conditions of employment and remuneration.

    Step 6: Offer letter will be issued to selected candidates. Candidates have to send a written acceptance to confirm their employment within 24 hours from the date of issue.

    Step 7: Appointment letter will be issued on the first day of joining PICT Model School. If a candidate fails to report to duty on the first day without prior notification, the appointment will stand cancelled thereof.

List of Documents Required

  1. School Leaving Certificate
  2. Pass Certificate & Mark Sheet of Grade 12
  3. Pass Certificate & Mark Sheet of Graduation / Highest examination passed
  4. Pass Certificate & Mark Sheet of B.Ed.
  5. Pass Certificate & Mark Sheet of statutory training for Language Teaching, if applicable
  6. Appointment order / document stating the current remuneration and post held
  7. PAN Card
  8. Aadhar card
  9. Residence Proof (if residing in own house else rent agreement)
  10. Relieving Order from the current organization
  11. Testimonials from previous employers
  12. Any other relevant document

We value time. Therefore, prior appointment is appreciated. Candidates have to carry one set of self-attested photocopy of the above mentioned documents. Originals will be required for verification. The entire procedure may take at least half a day.

The Heart of the Game

At PICT Model School, we believe physical health is as essential as education for the holistic development of our students. Sports are not just games; they are lessons in character, perseverance, and teamwork. Our comprehensive program builds a direct connection to a healthy body and a resilient mind, preparing students to overcome any challenge.

Through sport, students learn to handle victory and defeat with grace, enhance their strategic thinking, and build lifelong friendships. We are committed to fostering an environment where every child can discover their potential, both on and off the field.

Security

Surveillance

PICT Model School pays utmost attention towards safety and security of all students under its care. The campus is equipped with CCTV cameras in the common areas to ensure constant surveillance which is monitored at all times. Carrying identity cards is compulsory for all students and staff. Visitors need to make entries at security and are issued ID cards too before entering the campus. Visitors are escorted by security into the campus to the person they need to visit. All the classes are monitored by teachers at all times. Housekeeping staff and other helpers are always available, especially during break timings. Regular patrolling of common areas and washrooms during break time and dispersal is ensured. The young students are accompanied by the housekeeping ladies and frequently by the teachers, for rest room breaks, to ensure they are taken care of. Trained security personnel including lady guards within the campus ensure the safety of students throughout the day. The school adheres to all safety norms as prescribed by the regulatory authorities.

Anti-Bully Policy

The school also has an Anti-Bully Policy in place. Learners are made aware of these policies in class assembly. Regular positive reinforcement of the accepted norms by the educators for social behaviour ensures that learners study and grow in a healthy and safe environment. Regular awareness drives are conducted to sensitise the learners. The School's Anti Bullying Guidelines are appended below:


  1. Physical Bullying: Hitting, kicking, pushing, punching or any use of violence.
  2. Verbal Bullying: Name calling, teasing, insulting, sarcasm, writing unkind notes, spreading rumours, threats etc.
  3. Emotional Bullying: Being unfriendly, excluding, pressurizing, taking or hiding belongings etc.
  4. Cyber Bullying: All types of text messages, chat room misuse or any misuse of technology to cause harm to another.

If you are facing any of the above here is what you can do:

  • Talk to your Homeroom Teacher or anyone you trust.
  • Put a note in the POCSO box placed in the washroom.
  • Be part of a group. Do not remain by yourself when moving around in the school.
  • If you are scared to tell your teacher take a friend with you when you speak to teacher.
  • Remember you are not alone. Don’t suffer in silence.
  • You are not to be blamed for what is happening.

What can you do if you see someone else being bullied?

  • Get help of an adult the moment you see someone being bullied.
  • Encourage the child being bullied to talk to someone.
  • Try and be friends with the child who is being bullied.
  • Do not laugh or smile at the situation.
  • Don’t take on the bully yourself.

In case any bullying incident is reported, a fair investigation will be conducted by the school authorities. Depending on the gravity of the misconduct any of the actions below may be initiated:

  • Oral or written warning
  • Suspension from attending classes
  • Suspension from school for a specified period
  • Imposition of a fine
  • In the rarest of rare case, a bully may also be asked to take a transfer.

  • International Exposure - Cambridge English exams expose students to international English and testing methods, broadening their global perspective.
  • Visa Recognition - Select Cambridge English exams are recognized for visa purposes, serving as an alternative to exams like IELTS, among others.
  • Global Recognition - These exams are recognized in over 130 countries, by 20,000 organisations, and have been taken by more than 5 million candidates worldwide.
  • Lifelong Validity - The certificates obtained through these exams remain valid for life and are internationally accepted for work, study, and visa purposes.
  • International Standards - Parents can have confidence that their children are being taught English to internationally recognized standards.

BYE-LAWS

1. DEFINITION & AIM OF THE PTA

Parent Teachers Association (PTA) is a non-profit, non-political and non-sectarian organisation made up of school staff and parents which work to support the school in a wide variety of ways including improvement and development of the School. The PTA is formed in accordance with the Maharashtra Educational Institutions (Regulation of Fee) Act, 2011and the Rules made thereunder.

DEFINITION OF KEYWORDS

Association: All Parents and Teachers of PICT Model School.

Members: Any/All individuals who have been accepted and admitted by the Association.

Executive Committee: The Committee in which the management of the Association is vested i.e. elected parents, appointed teacher representative, Principal chosen by the School. Out of the total members of the Executive Committee, there shall be at least one member from the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes or Backward Class of citizens to be appointed by rotation so that every category gets representation in every year. At least 50% of the members shall be women.

PREAMBLE

We desire to sustain the promotion and continuity of sound, meaningful and qualitative education for the students of PICT Model School, we, the parents/guardians and teachers of the students hereby jointly and severely agree to constitute ourselves into an organization whose membership shall embrace all parents, guardians, and teachers of registered pupils in PICT Model School.

2. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES

The aims and objectives of the association shall be:

  1. To provide the platform for parents, guardians, and teachers of students of PICT MODEL SCHOOL to meet, exchange, deeply analyze issues, make recommendations and effectively pursue the implementation of decisions on matters affecting education / learning in PICT MODEL SCHOOL with appropriate agencies.
  2. To foster mutual understanding, harmonious relationship and cooperation among parents, guardians, and teachers in the fulfillment of their common aim, the welfare of the school and the pupils/students therein.
  3. To make for a healthy and sympathetic understanding of the education policies and programs of the school and thus influence the same to create a suitable climate for the reception of the same.

3. MEMBERSHIP OF PTA, QUALIFICATION

Membership of the association shall be open to:

  1. Parents / guardians whose children or wards attend school in PICT MODEL SCHOOL. Such participation shall be non-political and non-religious.
  2. Any person who is a member of the teaching staff of PICT MODEL SCHOOL.

4. EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE

The composition of the Executive Committee shall be:

  • Chairman- Principal of the school
  • Vice-Chairman – One from amongst the parents
  • Secretary –One from amongst the teachers
  • Two Joint Secretaries- Both from amongst the parents
  • Members – 1 Parent and 1 Teacher from every standard.

5. GUIDELINES AND RULES OF CONDUCT

  1. Members, will at all times, during its deliberation and actions, work with proper conduct and respect to one another and to the School.
  2. Each member must attend general meetings unless a member has a sound reason that will hinder him.
  3. Executive Committee will not concern themselves in individual / personal matters.
  4. Members shall be immediately terminated on the following grounds:
    • If a member is found acting prejudicially to the interest and working of the School and/or towards other members. Sufficient opportunity will be given to the member to submit an explanation. Final decision will be made by the School.
    • Any office holder of the association who goes into or intends to or is invited to or elected into partisan politics shall resign his PTA post or be requested to resign and vacate his post. Under no circumstances shall anyone involve the association into partisan politics.
    • If a member's child/children leave(s) the school.
    • If a member's employment at school is terminated.

6. SELECTION PROCESS

  1. The school shall select the Chairman, Secretary and Teacher representatives of the PTA. Vice Chairman can be nominated from the selected parent representatives.
  2. The Executive Committee shall be selected by lottery system method if more than one parent representative volunteers from each level within 30 days of the commencement of the academic session.
  3. A list of parents per Class level who had submitted their willingness to be a member of the Executive Committee, shall be compiled and kept for future use, in case of a resignation or termination of a selected parent.
  4. If a selected parent tenders his resignation in writing to PICT Model School, his children leave the school or are terminated, then a new member will be selected from those who stood in the Executive Committee nomination process OR any vacancy occurring in the executive committee of the association before another selection may be filled by a special meeting provided that the Chairman on the advice of the executive members may appoint any member to fill such a vacant post until a substantive holder is selected.
  5. Parents will be notified via circular of selected members of the Executive Committee for the PTA. Contact details and circular will be posted on the PICT MODEL SCHOOL website under PTA.
  6. In the event of any officer vacating his/her office before or due to another selection, he/she shall immediately hand over the properties of the association to the Chairman. The association shall be in order to seek police assistance, where such vacating officer refuses to hand over the properties.

7. THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE

  1. The Executive Committee will meet when necessary but, at least, once in every three months.
  2. The committee meetings are not open for nonmembers. However, PTA members may refer any relevant matter of their interest through the Secretary of the Association or through the Class Parent Representative, for discussions at these meetings.
  3. Decisions will be made by majority vote process.
  4. All committee members have equal voting rights, with the exception of the Chair, who has an additional casting vote, should this be needed.
  5. One third of the total strength of the Executive Committee shall constitute a quorum and more than 50% of the parent members shall be present at the Executive committee meetings. Without a quorum, no business shall be transacted.
  6. A selected member of the Committee shall cease to be a member of the Committee if the member fails to attend 3 consecutive meetings of the Committee.

8. GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT LIMITED TO

  • Help School in any events outside and beyond standard School functions such as: organizing intra school quiz competitions, science fair, community outreach, teacher appreciation event etc.
  • Work with the Parent Volunteer System to plan activities that support the vision and mission of the school.
  • Provide an "ear" to the issues concerning the parent body at large and take it up with School management for satisfactory resolution.
  • Solicit new ideas and suggestions from the parent body to help enhance the overall and all round education experience and work with PICT MODEL SCHOOL for review and implementation of the same.
  • Build a sense of community at school through increased and sustained parental participation and involvement in school events.
  • The Committee has the responsibility of approving the school fees as proposed by the Management within a period of 30 days after the proposal has been submitted by the management to the Executive Committee.
  • Foster a relationship between parents, teachers, school management and Board of Trustees.

9. CHANGE IN RULES AND REGULATIONS OF THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE

  1. Rules and regulations / roles and responsibilities will be constantly evolving and subject to review and changes based on the changing needs of Children, Parent, the School and the Teachers.
  2. Any changes in the Rules and Regulations must be approved at the Executive Committee meeting.

Dear Madam
It is a privilege to have our child go to PICT. It was exemplified by the amount of planning and preparation that had gone into and behind the scenes. More importantly, balancing safety and enjoyment is quite a tightrope and I must acknowledge that this was perfectly balanced by each one of the staff at PICT. There were times when children were quite tired of the unending briefings and there was a lot of commotion in WhatsApp groups expressing angst and displeasure, but with the advantage of hindsight, I would be the first to admit that each act by the school, each diktat and each guideline issued, were singularly responsible to make the trip a safe environment for the learners.
The choice of location and the depth of information given to the learners is also commendable. When Anagha excitedly pointed out that we had skipped Nathmal ki Haveli on our trip earlier, and the details around how its twin architects went about decorating the haveli until the two met, or the Shringar Chowk or the 300 Jalis inside Mehrangarh, it really is a testament to how learning should be conducted in a school. Without rambling further, I would like to end this note with a deep sense of appreciation and also urge you to ignore any snide comments or negative feedback from any quarter because the only thing that I can say with certainty, is that a trip of such a magnitude couldn’t have been possible without a very determined set of folks at the helm providing unwavering direction.

Vijay & Dr. Anuradha Subramaniam
